newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Profit pushes Wesfarmers to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Profit pushes Wesfarmers to new highs.

text.p: Shares in agricultural, energy and hardware group Wesfarmers Ltd touched a record high of A$13.00 on Wednesday as traders expressed approval of Tuesday's results.

The Western Australian-based group reported a 50 percent lift in net profit to A$139.55 million for the year ending June 30 and boosted the final dividend to 38 cents per share from 20 cents per share.
"They are back to their highs. It was certainly a strong result," a Sydney-based dealer said.
The company said its upbeat performance should continue, with further growth in revenue and earnings expected in the 1997/98 financial year.
Strong growth in 1997/98 would be generated from the expanding hardware warehouse chain with the expected upturn in the housing market to also lift earnings, Wesfarmers said.
Wesfarmers' 51 percent shareholder, The Franked Income Fund, felt the flow effect from a bullish tone in Wesfarmers shares.
Its units also hit a record high, peaking at A$4.11 before easing back to be nine cents higher at A$4.09 on turnover of 355,396 units by 11.40 a.m. (0140 GMT).
At the same time, Wesfarmers shares were back from their highs to be up 35 cents at A$12.95 on turnover of 65,466 shares.
